# r4.0-pre.11

- Windows synchronization now keeps each source file open through transfer and response cleanup, avoiding repeated post-transfer path/parent opens. This applies to initial upload and watched updates; no diagnostic feature or special setting is required.
- While a file is being transferred, another application's attempt to replace or delete that file may fail. Retry after the transfer completes or synchronization stops. In-place editing remains possible; observed size/mtime changes cause a rescan/resend.
- Changing read permissions after a source was opened does not revoke its already granted handle: the current transfer can finish. Planned remote deletions still require a fresh local readability/root check; a failed check stops deletion. This differs from pre.10 for some large-file permission changes.
- A generated-localhost actual-GUI comparison of 4,000 small 512-byte files, deletion ON and empty destinations measured the trial at 8.11 seconds median versus WinSCP's approximate 10.32 to 11.41-second median bounds (3 runs each). Nearly used button-event to completion-DOM plus two animation frames; WinSCP used native click bounds and a seconds-granularity visible log. Observation overhead/precision differ; this is not a real-server or universal speed guarantee.

Existing comparison/deletion policy and small direct writes/large fresh staging remain as in pre.10. Small-file partial contents can be visible during transfer; no foreign partial resume was added. Uncertain network/cleanup outcomes are still errors. Same-size edits with exactly restored timestamps are not guaranteed detectable.

Prerelease; stable Latest remains r3.6. No Explorer drag/drop migration or unrelated visual changes are included.
